cases.question: At the declared captured-cDNA amplification scope, do these connected regions share the biotin/streptavidin capture, bead-bound template-switch and five-cycle PCR-to-soluble-product mechanism, and which substrate/primer/identity differences limit a common definition?

operations.name: Capture biotin-tagged cDNAs
operations.action: Prepare streptavidin beads, thaw/adjust the lysate, inhibit Proteinase K with PMSF, bind cDNAs to the beads with rotation and wash the retained bead fraction.
operations.information_effect: Enriches biotin-B-tagged cDNA without intentionally selecting RNA over ADT products; retains addresses and molecule tags.

operations.name: Add the second PCR handle
operations.action: Resuspend captured cDNAs in template-switch reaction mix, incubate, then magnetically rinse the retained beads.
operations.information_effect: Adds an amplification handle to the target-derived end while retaining the spatial/UMI end.

operations.name: Five-cycle PCR and bead removal
operations.action: Amplify on the cleaned beads using primers 1/2 plus primer 3 for the joint protein route; remove beads magnetically after five cycles and retain the soluble product.
operations.information_effect: Amplifies RNA- and ADT-derived products while retaining the barcoding/target associations; magnetic beads do not enter the second-PCR solution.

boundary_inputs.description: Collected lysate from the gasket-defined barcoded tissue region, containing spatially tagged mRNA- and ADT-derived cDNAs; may be stored at −80°C.

internal_handoffs.description: Washed streptavidin bead-bound biotin-tagged cDNAs recovered from the lysate; both mRNA and ADT products remain in the joint path.
Washed bead-bound cDNA after template switching adds the other PCR handle, retaining spatial A/B tags, UMI and transcript/ADT identity.

boundary_outputs.description: Five-cycle PCR solution after magnetic bead removal; soluble RNA/ADT amplicons, distinct from discarded magnetic beads.

operations.name: Capture and wash biotin-associated cDNA
operations.action: Prepare streptavidin beads, thaw sublibrary lysates, inhibit residual proteinase K with PMSF, bind cDNA to beads and wash the retained bead fraction.
operations.information_effect: Retains cDNA via the biotin/streptavidin capture interface introduced by the third barcode assembly, while preserving per-tube sublibrary assignment.

operations.name: Template-switch bead-bound cDNA
operations.action: Incubate cDNA-bearing streptavidin beads with Maxima RT and the modified template-switch oligo BC_0127. The consequential output is switched cDNA for subsequent PCR; the packet does not specify the complete new-end sequence.
operations.information_effect: Provides the template-switch interface used for amplification alongside the previously added universal barcode-side PCR handle; exact strand-end reconstruction remains unresolved.

operations.name: Amplify five cycles and remove beads
operations.action: Wash the template-switch beads, amplify cDNA for five PCR cycles, remove Dynabeads from the PCR solution, and add EvaGreen for monitored continuation.
operations.information_effect: Amplifies production cDNA while retaining barcode/UMI identities; bead removal creates the soluble material interface for qPCR-monitored continuation.

boundary_inputs.description: Separate frozen sublibrary lysates after SDS/proteinase K treatment and reversal of formaldehyde crosslinks; biotin-tagged, three-round-barcoded cDNA and its UMI remain associated with each physical sublibrary.

internal_handoffs.description: Per-sublibrary streptavidin beads with retained biotin-associated barcoded cDNA after magnetic capture and washes; the unbound lysate fraction is not the production cDNA path.

Bead-bound, barcoded cDNA after the reported template-switch reaction with BC_0127. The switch supplies the complementary end needed for the following BC_0062/BC_0108 amplification; exact handle sequence/structure is unavailable in the packet.

boundary_outputs.description: Sublibrary cDNA amplification product after five PCR cycles, with Dynabeads removed; this soluble PCR fraction enters monitored amplification.

cases.question: Can one DBiT library-construction operation correspond to the two connected SPLiT tagmentation/index-PCR operations at the named Nextera-XT cDNA-to-sequencing-library boundary, while retaining differences in documented indexing and unspecified DBiT internals?

operations.name: Build RNA library by tagmentation
operations.action: Build the mRNA-derived sequencing library with Nextera XT, at the published kit boundary. Tagmentation is reported, but internal fragmentation/end-repair/index-PCR settings are not specified in the frozen packet and are not invented.
operations.information_effect: Converts the RNA cDNA fraction to paired-end-sequenceable molecules while retaining spatial-code/UMI and transcript identities at the supported kit boundary.

boundary_inputs.description: RNA-derived cDNA retained for Nextera XT construction after the reported Qubit/Bioanalyzer assessment. Analytical sampling amount and remaining production fraction are unspecified; this is not a perfect copy of the premeasurement material.

boundary_outputs.description: mRNA-derived sequencing library made from the >300 bp fraction with Nextera XT tagmentation; retains spatial barcode/UMI end and transcript information for paired-end reading. Exact selected RNA adapter/index identity is not specified.

operations.name: Tagment and neutralize
operations.action: Apply the reported Nextera XT tagmentation to the 600 pg cDNA aliquot and neutralize before library PCR. The molecular processing is represented at the named kit boundary; no unreported kit adapter sequence or enzyme architecture is assigned.
operations.information_effect: Creates the reported tagmented library substrate. Amplification before tagmentation means different sequenced portions of the same original transcript can retain one UMI-UBC identity.

operations.name: Round 4: index PCR and library cleanup
operations.action: Amplify the neutralized tagmentation mixture with P5 and one selected indexed P7 primer to assign sublibrary identity. Remove 40 μL from the PCR and purify that retained portion using 0.7× SPRI beads.
operations.information_effect: Introduces the fourth barcode as the selected sublibrary sequencing index, retains the first-three well labels/UMI, and produces sequencing-compatible material.

boundary_inputs.description: 600 pg physical aliquot of 0.8× SPRI-purified production cDNA, diluted in water to 5 μL for tagmentation. This is the retained amount entering the library route, rather than the entire purified pool.

internal_handoffs.description: Neutralized Nextera XT-tagmented cDNA derived from the 600 pg sublibrary aliquot, before the indexed library PCR. The source names the kit boundary without reporting internal adapter/end sequences.

boundary_outputs.description: Illumina-compatible purified sublibrary material after index PCR: the retained product comes from 40 μL of the PCR reaction purified with 0.7× SPRI beads. One selected indexed P7 primer (one of BC_0076–BC_0083 in the listed recipe) establishes the fourth, sublibrary identity; P5 is BC_0118. Existing cDNA/barcode/UMI identities are retained in the sequenced molecules.

cases.question: Does the shared tagmentation name justify common whole-transform membership when ATAC converts chromatin accessibility into genomic fragment selection, whereas SPLiT prepares already amplified barcoded cDNA for sequencing?

operations.name: Tagment native chromatin
operations.action: Immediately resuspend nuclei in the transposition mix. Adapter-loaded hyperactive Tn5 simultaneously fragments and tags DNA by integrating its sequencing-adapter payload; steric hindrance makes insertion less probable in less accessible chromatin. Incubate as reported. Keep standard and low-cell reaction volumes distinct. The paper attributes insertion of two adapters separated by 9 bp at each dimeric target event to previous Tn5 descriptions; this target-event spacing is distinct from paired-fragment insert length.
operations.information_effect: Converts physical accessibility into preferential adapter-bearing genomic fragments. The paired insertion positions and retained insert lengths subsequently encode accessibility, protected factor sites and nucleosome-scale protection.

boundary_inputs.description: Native nuclei pellet retained after cold lysis and centrifugation, standard route.
Native nuclei pellet from 500 or 5,000 input cells. The low-cell section inherits nuclei preparation from the common protocol; this is not a claim of complete physical recovery.

boundary_outputs.description: Standard-route transposed chromatin/DNA sample before cleanup: fragmented genomic DNA carrying integrated sequencing-adapter payloads, enriched for accessible regions. Original molecular insert identities and lengths are the information carrier; exact commercial loaded-adapter duplex/end structure is not specified.
Unpurified 5 μL low-cell transposition reaction, carrying the adapter-tagged genomic fragments; transferred directly into PCR, retaining this route identity.

operations.name: Tagment and neutralize
operations.action: Apply the reported Nextera XT tagmentation to the 600 pg cDNA aliquot and neutralize before library PCR. The molecular processing is represented at the named kit boundary; no unreported kit adapter sequence or enzyme architecture is assigned.

cases.question: Do nucleotide conversion and subsequent primed synthesis describe the same transformation in SLAM and scBS, after accounting for RNA/DNA substrate, reacting base, chemistry, synthesis enzyme and encoded biological information?

operations.name: Carboxyamidomethylate s4U and recover RNA
operations.action: React total RNA with iodoacetamide, covalently attaching a carboxyamidomethyl group to s4U through nucleophilic substitution. Quench with excess DTT and recover the treated RNA by ethanol precipitation.
operations.information_effect: Changes s4U covalent identity so that reverse transcription reports the label as T>C substitutions; no physical labeled-RNA purification is introduced.

operations.name: Initiate Quant-seq first-strand synthesis
operations.action: Within the manufacturer-directed Quant-seq construction, prime polyadenylated RNA with the oligo-dT-anchor primer containing an Illumina-compatible linker and synthesize first-strand cDNA. Reverse-transcription-dependent recoding carries the alkylated-s4U signal into the library.
operations.information_effect: Selects polyadenylated transcript 3′ regions by priming and records s4U-dependent altered base recognition through reverse transcription. This implementation reports Pol II RNA kinetics and 3′ isoform identity; splice isoforms are unresolved.

boundary_inputs.description: Total RNA extracted at the selected pulse, chase or no-s4U control time point, with DTT protection. Labeled and unlabeled RNA remain together; source route, biological condition and time identity are kept separately for each sample.

internal_handoffs.description: Recovered ethanol-precipitated total RNA in which s4U thiol groups have been covalently carboxyamidomethylated by iodoacetamide. This chemically modified RNA remains mixed with RNA lacking s4U and is the Quant-seq input.

boundary_outputs.description: Quant-seq first-strand reaction product: oligo-dT-anchor-primed cDNA carrying the primer-associated Illumina-compatible linker, before the reported RNA-removal/second-strand step. This is a conceptual interface within the manufacturer-directed construction, not an isolated aliquot.

operations.name: Bisulfite-convert, fragment and recover DNA
operations.action: Apply the modified Imprint conversion to lysate DNA before adapter addition, causing fragmentation and conversion of unmethylated cytosines. Purify by the cited PBAT recovery boundary and elute. Apply the assay boundary independently to each concomitant negative-control tube; no tubes are merged here.
operations.information_effect: Encode the source’s unmethylated-cytosine conversion while fragmenting DNA; recover converted fragments before adapters are introduced. Tube and control identity remain separate.

operations.name: Five rounds of first-adapter priming and extension
operations.action: Random-prime converted fragments with biotin-bearing oligo1 and extend complementary strands; denature and replenish primer, enzyme and nucleotides for subsequent rounds, for five rounds in total.
operations.information_effect: Add the first Illumina-adapter-derived sequence by synthesis, with a 3′ random-nine priming tract and 5′ biotin tag; generate repeated copies before the second adapter is added.

boundary_inputs.description: Individually mouth-picked MII oocyte lysate, 12μl final, with oocyte-specific lysis treatment; one cell’s identity retained.
Single sorted live low-DNA-content G0/G1 E14 ESC in 12μl ESC lysis buffer after lysis; its serum/2i provenance remains associated with the tube.
Separately labeled negative-control tube: lysis buffer alone or sorted BD Accudrop Beads. Prepared and processed with the single-cell tubes; contains no intentionally supplied cell.

internal_handoffs.description: Per separately processed tube, retaining single-cell specimen identity or matched negative-control identity; recovered fragmented bisulfite-converted DNA in 10mM Tris-Cl pH 8.5, before adapter incorporation; negative tubes represent any recoverable background material.

boundary_outputs.description: Per separately processed tube, retaining single-cell specimen identity or matched negative-control identity; reaction containing first-adapter-tagged complementary copies of converted fragments, primed by 5′ biotin-bearing oligo1 with a 3′ random-nine tract, after five rounds. The source describes multiple copies per fragment.

When processing one sorted E14 ESC tube.
When processing a matched buffer-only or sorted-bead negative-control tube.
